groups.activity: kill enemy Necramechs for Matrices; rank Necraloid to 3 (Odima)
groups.meta: T1 (one Necramech) drops Orientation, T2 (two) Ballistics, T3 (three) Animus

rows.label: Necraloid Rank 1
rows.note: 5,000 standing, 10 Orientation Matrix, 150 Void Traces, Zymos Barrel Blueprint, 20 Father Tokens

rows.label: Necraloid Rank 2
rows.note: 22,000 standing, 15 Ballistics Matrix, 250 Void Traces, Sepulcrum Barrel Blueprint, 20 Father Tokens

rows.label: Necraloid Rank 3, Odima
rows.note: 44,000 standing, 15 Animus Matrix, 350 Void Traces, Trumna Barrel Blueprint, 20 Father Tokens

conditions: Farm matrices by killing enemy Necramechs, not by hoping for bounty completion rewards — each kill drops a matrix of the tier's type.
Trade Orokin Matrices to Loid for standing: Orientation 1,000, Ballistics 2,500, Animus 5,000 each.
bonuses: Nekros Desecrate paired with a drop booster and Resourceful Retriever boosts matrix drops.
Go public rather than solo — matchmade vault lobbies are trivial, and Sporothrix/Arum Spinosa farm groups run vaults constantly.
It speeds up as you go: higher tiers spawn more Necramechs, so matrix income scales with what each rank demands.

disclosures.title: unverified
disclosures.body: Whether Loid's matrix trade-ins count against the daily standing cap wasn't confirmed.

conditions: The Rank 3 free reward is a single pick — take Cortege's blueprint free and buy Morgha's for 8,000 standing, or vice versa.
Vault rotations cycle every 2.5 hours (A-B-C), so if you're farming the damaged parts instead of buying them, a missing one can be up to 5 hours away.
bonuses: Buying the Damaged parts from Loid skips the 3% rotation-locked vault RNG entirely.
